dicas.texto: Você está indo bem! Se cada pacote tem 5 peças, quantas peças formam exatamente um pacote inteiro?
Tente dividir o total de peças (6) pelo tamanho do pacote (5). Quantas vezes o 5 cabe no 6 e quanto sobra?
Você tem 6 peças. Você pode tirar um grupo de 5 para formar 1 inteiro. Quantas peças sobram fora desse grupo?
O número misto terá 1 inteiro (o pacote completo) e uma fração com o que sobrou sobre o total de 5. Tente colocar 1 em m1 e o resto em m2/m3.
Lembre-se que cada unidade na reta está dividida em 5 partes. Onde fica o 1 inteiro nessa reta?
Comece no zero, conte 5 tracinhos para chegar no 1, e depois conte mais um tracinho para representar a parte que sobrou.
O ponto deve ficar um pouquinho depois do número 1 na reta. Tente clicar na primeira marca após o 1.
Se cada marca vale 1/5, conte 6 marcas a partir do zero. Onde esse ponto cai?

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; pergunta "What is the fraction in the problem? Convert it to mixed fraction form if it will help you." com duas caixas numéricas (f1 em cima = numerador, f2 embaixo = denominador); botão "Convert" que abre as caixas do número misto (m1 = parte inteira, m2/m3 = fração restante; "-" quando não há); reta numérica de 0 a 2 (numline) onde o aluno marca um ponto, com encaixe em 5 partes por unidade (marcas ocultas); texto de apoio na reta: "The number hint is off in this problem!"; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (digitar nos campos, converter, marcar o ponto, concluir).

dicas.texto: In a fraction, the numerator tells how many pieces are being described.
Look at the number of gum pieces Brandon gave to Luke and enter that quantity in the top box.
The top box should show the number of pieces given, not the number of pieces in one pack.
Count the pieces Brandon gave Luke and type that count into the numerator box.
The denominator describes the size of one whole group.
Find how many gum pieces are in a single pack, then enter that quantity in the bottom box.
Use the number of pieces per pack, not the number Brandon gave away.
Read the sentence about each pack and type that group size into the denominator box.
Compare the number of pieces described with the number of pieces that make one complete pack.
A fraction is greater than one when its numerator is larger than its denominator.
Check whether the top number is greater than, equal to, or less than the bottom number.
Set the fraction model so it represents the given pieces divided into groups the size of one pack.
A mixed number separates complete groups from the remaining part of a group.
Divide the numerator by the denominator to find the complete groups and the remainder.
Use the number of complete groups for the whole-number box, and use the leftover pieces over the original group size for the fraction.
Click Convert, enter the complete-group count, then enter the leftover-piece count over the pack size.
Use the number line to locate the amount between the nearby whole numbers.
Divide the numerator by the denominator to convert the fraction into a decimal location.
The interval from 1 to 2 is divided into five equal parts, so each step represents one fifth.
Start at 1 and move one equal fifth-sized interval to the right.
Check that all representations describe the same quantity of gum packs.
Compare the fraction, the mixed number, and the marked location before submitting.
Make sure the point is between 1 and 2 and that it matches the remaining fractional part.
Review every visible field and the marked point, then press the Done button.

exercicio.statement:
Brandon had packs of gum that he shared with his friend. Each pack had five pieces. He gave Luke six pieces. Describe the number of packs of gum Brandon gave away and show the value on the number line.
What is the fraction in the problem? Convert it to mixed fraction form if it will help you.

steps.instruction: Enter the number of pieces Brandon gave in the top fraction box.
Enter the number of pieces in one pack in the bottom fraction box.
Use the fraction model to show that the fraction is greater than one.
Click Convert and represent the fraction as a mixed number.
Mark 6/5 on the number line from 0 to 2.
Click Done after checking that your fraction and point agree.

Start at 1 and move one equal fifth-sized interval to the right.
